speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the recent camping trip in Minnesota and the self-resolving knee pain are significant clues. Has the skin lesions appeared on your body recently, and do you have any other symptoms like joint swelling or difficulty moving other joints?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and Blood Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up photograph of the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands.

Based on the painful, tender wrists with "punched-out" appearing lesions and the history of a self-resolving knee issue, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of a specific tick-borne infection. Are you aware of any tick bites during your camping trip in Minnesota?
